stem: A fair coin is tossed five times. What is the probability of getting exactly three heads?

verdicts.working: There are 2^5 = 32 equally likely outcomes. Exactly three heads can occur in C(5,3) = 10 ways, so the probability is 10/32 = 5/16.

working:
$P(X=3)=\binom{5}{3}\left(\dfrac12\right)^3\left(\dfrac12\right)^2$\n$=\dfrac{10}{32}=\dfrac{5}{16}$.

Independent check: There are 2^5 = 32 equally likely outcomes. Exactly three heads can occur in C(5,3) = 10 ways, so the probability is 10/32 = 5/16.
solution:
The number of ways to get exactly three heads is $\binom{5}{3}$ out of $2^5$ equally likely outcomes.
$$P(X=3)=\frac{\binom{5}{3}}{2^5}=\frac{10}{32}=\frac{5}{16}$$
